A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ensemble-agreement cascading work, renamed from CoE to ABC. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original accuracy–FLOPs comparisons, simulated hardware and communication costs, and appendix analyses of incorrect agreements and parallel execution.

after.justification: v2 retains original cascading results and adds API-based experiments, threshold-estimation studies, and selection-rate analyses.

M1.justification: The ensemble cascade is retained under the name ABC. Beyond v1's voting-threshold procedure, v2 explicitly permits deferral using average ensemble prediction scores (Equation 4) and introduces validation-based threshold selection in Appendix B.

E1.justification: v2 retains the five original benchmarks and adds GSM8K, COQA, OVERRULING, and HEADLINES. These extend evaluation to mathematical reasoning, conversational QA, legal reasoning, and news classification through black-box model APIs (Section 5.2.3 and Table 2).

E2.justification: WoC and best-single-model comparisons are retained. v2 additionally evaluates FrugalGPT, AutoMix+T, AutoMix+P, and MoT LLM Cascade in Figure 5; these were not evaluated in v1. HybridLLM and other newly discussed routers are not counted as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The new API experiments introduce two- and three-tier configurations, four-shot prompting, COQA macro F1, and exact-match accuracy for the other tasks. v2 also introduces validation-based threshold calibration and describes edge-to-cloud evaluation as two-level, whereas v1 assigned increasing delays across cascade tiers; this documentation does not establish reruns.

E4.justification: v2 adds sensitivity analyses of relative model cost and parallelism (Figure 3), threshold stability versus sample count (Figure 6), and selection rates under different error tolerances (Figure 7). It removes v1's wrong-agreement analysis and Table 3, cascade-exit histograms, and standalone ensemble-gain comparison. The parallel-versus-sequential Figure 8 is retained.

E5.justification: Appendix B newly specifies plug-in estimation of failure probability from validation samples and examines estimation stability as sample counts increase. Neither version reports evaluation-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the added calibration analysis does not establish repeated experimental runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds API accuracy/F1–cost results and threshold/selection-rate findings, while removing v1's incorrect-agreement counts and annotated ensemble gains. The original benchmark curves are largely redisplayed, and every per-tier numerical entry in v1 Table 2 is retained in v2 Table 5; these are not new performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 replaces v1's oracle/Bayes-deferral treatment with an accuracy-constrained cascade formulation, safe-deferral definition, parallelism cost model, and Proposition 4.1. Appendices A–B add excess-risk derivations and threshold-estimation mathematics. The new cost expressions are internally inconsistent: Equation 1 uses k^(1-rho), whereas Proposition 4.1 uses k^rho.

C1.justification: v2 adds an explicit theoretical contribution concerning safe deferral and accuracy-preserving replacement, plus a headline claim of 2–25× API-price savings. v1 emphasized up to 7× inference-cost reduction with parallel execution. The training-free cascading claim and approximately 3× GPU and 14× communication savings remain.

C2.justification: v2 substantially explains how cost ratios, parallelism, and selection rates govern savings, including cases where cascading costs more. It adds explanations involving FrugalGPT deferrals and AutoMix verification overhead, while removing v1's interpretation of wrong agreements. Section 5.2.2 also overgeneralizes GPU savings to at least 3× for image tasks despite the retained ImageNet numbers.

D1.justification: v2 provides API checkpoint names, tier assignments, and token prices in Table 1, plus model/dataset inventories and detailed baseline setup instructions in Appendix D.2. These include AutoMix sampling temperature and eight verification calls, router training-sample requirements, and FrugalGPT's DistilBERT scorer. Appendix B adds threshold-calibration instructions.

R1.justification: Related work substantially expands coverage of LLM routing, including HybridLLM, OrchestraLLM, RouteLLM, and other routers, alongside additional scaling-law and heterogeneous-serving literature. v2 sharpens its positioning around accuracy-constrained replacement versus budget-constrained cascading. The WILLUMP discussion is removed; historical face-detection positioning is retained.

P1.justification: The paper is extensively rewritten and reorganized: CoE becomes ABC, an intuitive method overview precedes separate theoretical sections, experiments are organized around feasibility conditions and three deployment scenarios, and the appendices become Sections A–E. The abstract, contribution statement, and conclusion are substantially revised.

P2.justification: v2 expands Figure 1 with a scaling panel, redraws benchmark plots with logarithmic axes and consolidated legends, and combines the GPU-cost and latency figures. It adds API and sensitivity plots plus dataset/model tables, removes several earlier displays, and changes the abstract and appendix layouts. Figure 8 and the detailed cost table are relocated.

improvement.justification: The API comparisons, deployment qualifications, and reproducibility details strengthen v1's limited comparative evidence. However, v2 introduces conflicting cost formulas and overstates unchanged GPU results: Table 5 gives an ImageNet saving of 1.29/0.74, approximately 1.74×, despite Section 5.2.2 claiming at least 3× for image tasks. It also removes the wrong-agreement analysis. These gains and losses in evidential reliability leave the net quality direction uncertain.
